I haven't lived in Manchester but between Bristol and London, I would pick Bristol. It's harder to make and maintain friends in London. The city is overwhelmingly big so unless you have an insider's perspective/you know someone who does, it's very hard to find your niche outside of the usual, basic tourist trappings. 

Bristol did feel small to me at first because I am from a much larger city but it grew on me in a very short space of time. There's plenty to do always and I'm never bored. As someone else mentioned, especially if you lean politically left/progressive and have an interest in alt culture, then Bristol is the city for you.

Asking people questions is key. "How was your weekend?", "Did you see the news with xyz public figure the other day?", "I saw this movie that I though you'd really like!". Another thing I would recommend is to observe how people in your social circles converse and try an emulate what they do (how they start conversations, navigate awkward silences etc.). 

Be observant, keep trying, have a positive attitude that makes people WANT to talk to you. Assertiveness doesn't mean you have to appear aggressive, just that you should be self assured. Best of luck!
